title: The proton as a Borromean hadron
html:
Example. The proton as a Borromean hadron

The proton is a hadron. Its three constituents link in a Borromean configuration.

Constituent quarks as unknots. Quarks are unknots K_{0_1} distinguished by their crossing orientation within the Borromean link. The up quark \mathfrak{u} carries positive crossing orientation. The down quark \mathfrak{d} carries negative crossing orientation. The proton \mathfrak{p} comprises two up quarks and one down quark:

  \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p \oplus \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Bor}},

where \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Bor}} is the Borromean link.

Borromean property. The Borromean link requires all three components to remain linked. Removing any single component unlinks the remaining two:

  • Remove \mathfrak{u}_1: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_2, \mathfrak{d}) has linking number zero and separates.
  • Remove \mathfrak{u}_2: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{d}) unlinks.
  • Remove \mathfrak{d}: the pair (\mathfrak{u}_1, \mathfrak{u}_2) unlinks.

The three components form a non-trivial link. Their pairwise linking numbers vanish, but their Milnor triple linking number \bar{\mu}(123) = \pm 1 is non-zero. This provides the topological mechanism for quark confinement. No single quark can be extracted without dissolving the entire structure. Any two-body subsystem remains topologically trivial.

Mass from the linking matrix. The proton mass decomposes into constituent masses and binding energy:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} = 2\mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{u}) + \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{d}) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}.

The binding energy \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}} originates from the Borromean linking. Because the individual quark masses \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{u}) and \mathfrak{m}(\mathfrak{d}) are small, the binding energy dominates. The mass of the proton arises overwhelmingly from topological complexity.

We compute the binding energy from the crossing energy of the linking braid word \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} \in B_3. The Borromean link admits the braid representation \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} = (\sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1)^3. This geometry yields mutual crossings that ensure \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p}) < 0. At the substrate parameter q \approx 1.110, this evaluates to:

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}}(q) \approx 938.272\;\text{MeV} \text{MeV}.

Stability of the proton. The proton is the lightest baryon and cannot decay. Topologically, the Borromean link of three unknots is the simplest non-trivial three-component link carrying the correct charge and color quantum numbers. No sequence of Reidemeister moves or Markov stabilizations simplifies it further while preserving the baryon number.
